title: Adobe client ID, secret uuid, documented placeholders, references and masks beside no client secret value
summary: A client ID in an x-api-key header, a secret uuid in a delete path and a list response with no secret value, the documented {CLIENT_SECRET}, <YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET>, {AUTHORIZATION} and X-run placeholders, a public client request with a client_id only, an environment reference and a masked display.
rationale: The client ID is the credential's public identifier (sent as x-api-key and in the consent URL) and the secret uuid identifies a secret without being it: the list response returns only uuids and metadata. The pages show the secret only as the placeholders {CLIENT_SECRET}, <YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET>, {AUTHORIZATION} and a run of X characters (claims s2s-client-secret-docs-placeholders, enterprise-web-app-client-secret-placeholders-only, web-app-client-secret-placeholders-only), and a public client sends client_id and no secret. A reference or a mask stands in for a value kept elsewhere. Flagging any of these would redact documentation and identifiers a reader needs. The case covers all three Adobe client-secret families because the documented placeholders are shared. It decides nothing about org_id or the consent id_token (see the separate not-assertable case).

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are public identifiers, documented placeholders, references or masks, not credential values; that a placeholder, reference or mask is not a value is a project decision, not an Adobe statement. Adobe documents the client ID and secret uuid roles and shows the secret only as the listed placeholders.

sources.supports: client_id is the Client ID obtained from the Developer Console and is sent in the x-api-key header of the secrets API requests, separately from the client secret.
sources.locator: sections "Fetching access tokens" and "List all client secrets"

sources.supports: The consent URL carries client_id as a query parameter, described as the Client ID of the partner app from the credential overview page.

No client_secret values are returned by the list API, only the secret uuid and other metadata; the secret uuid is needed to delete a secret and the plain text client_secret cannot be used to identify which secret to delete.
sources.locator: sections "List all client secrets" and "Remove client secret from credential"

sources.supports: Sample responses for adding a client secret (client_secret shown as a run of X characters) and listing client secrets (uuid and metadata only); the page states no format for the value.
sources.locator: sections "Add client secret to credential" and "List all client secrets", Sample Response

sources.supports: Request examples use {CLIENT_SECRET} placeholders; the page states no format for the value.
Request examples use {AUTHORIZATION}; the parameter tables describe the header as Base64(clientId:clientSecret); no value format is stated.
sources.locator: sections "Fetching Access tokens" and "Refreshing Access tokens"

sources.supports: cURL request and sample response use <YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET> and "ey....." placeholders; id_token is described as a well formed JSON web token with claims iss, sub, aud, exp, iat, org_id and nonce.
sources.locator: sections "Generate Access Token Request" and "Redirect URL"
